newsitem.title: DUBAI: Poor local, Indian demand depress Dubai gold trade.
newsitem.headline: Poor local, Indian demand depress Dubai gold trade.

text.p: Trade in the Dubai gold souk slowed further in the week to Sunday, with gold traders reporting scant demand from India and Pakistan and weak local retail interest.
"The market is very, very dull. There is no physical demand from India or Pakistan," said one trader.

"Muharram is still going on and there is no (wedding or festival) season in India at the moment," he added, referring to the Moslem Muharram period which is a traditionally slow time for retail business.
It is considered by some Moslems to be one of the faith's holiest months and a period of reflection, even mourning.
The wedding season, usually a good time for gold sales, is almost over in the Indian subcontinent, spelling a slow down in sales until late in the third quarter, traders said.

They said with the start of summer, local jewellery demand had dried up. Traditionally, sales in the downtown gold souk slide with the start of the long, hot summer in May and business only starts picking up again in September and October when tourists and holidaying UAE residents return.
Prices in Dubai dropped in line with lower world bullion prices in the week. Dubai's benchmark ten tola bar was quoted at 4,738 dirhams ($1,291) on Sunday from 4,763 dirhams ($1,298) a week earlier.
The ten tola bar is 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold.
On the international spot market, gold was last quoted on Saturday at $342.50/343.00 an ounce from $344.30/80 a week earlier.
"The outlook is also pretty bleak. The international market is weak and there is no bullish news around to pull it higher," said a dealer.
